'''Jacques Denavit''' (1 October 1930 – 12 September 2013)<ref name=":llnl"/> was a physicist and professor of mechanical engineering.
Together with his teacher [[Richard S. Hartenberg]], he developed the [[DH parameters|Denavit-Hartenberg convention]] where one can calculate the [[forward kinematics]] of a [[kinematic chain]] using matrices.<ref name=":dmg"/><ref name=":kinnot"/> He joined the Department of Mechanical Engineering and Astronomical Science at [[Northwestern University|Northwestern]] in 1958. This is where Denavit started collaborating with [[Richard S. Hartenberg]]. Together, they introduced many concepts in kinematics of serial manipulators.<ref name=":rvc"/> Denavit was named a Fellow of the American Physical Society in 1977.<ref name=":llnl"/><ref name=":aps"/> He retired in 1982.<ref name=":rvc"/>

==Selected publications==
# A Kinematic Notation for Lower-Pair Mechanisms Based on Matrices (1955)<ref name=":kinnot"/>
# Kinematic Synthesis of Linkages (1964)<ref name=":kinsynth"/>
# Numerical simulation of plasmas with periodic smoothing in phase space (1972)<ref name=":simplasmas"/>
